messages:
maya: FYI customer (Acme Corp) seeing a regression after we rolled the canary this morning. latency up ~3x and intermittent 502s. shared 3 req ids: req_3a8f, req_3a91, req_3aef. asking for repro steps and whether pinning to stable will avoid it.

sam: thanks — can you drop a minimal curl repro we can give eng? also need a debug bundle + full request IDs (both api req-id header and our internal req ids).

maya: pasted what customer sent: 
Customer: "we call /v1/generate with model=redwood-xl-3:canary, we started seeing timeouts ~10:12am PDT"

maya: customer gave this curl (sanitized):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-3:canary","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":200}'
```

diego: quick checklist: 1) we need the full response headers (to see x-rw-reqid + backend trace id) 2) debug bundle from customer (collects client logs + req ids) 3) confirm routing policy for that tenant — if canary failure should fall back to stable.

lee: +1 on headers. ask customer to run curl with explicit x-request-id and capture response headers: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -H 'X-Request-ID: acme-20260315-01' \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-3:canary","input":"test","max_tokens":20}'
```

sam: also request they add our debug header so runtime emits extra traces: 
`-H 'X-RW-Debug: 1'`
and attach the raw response (headers + body).

maya: asking customer now for that. they want to know if we can just pin them back to stable while we investigate.

diego: you can pin at the tenant-level via the pin API. quick command to pin them to stable variant: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/acme/pins \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_KEY>' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-xl-3","priority":"sticky"}'
```
note: this sets a tenant-level sticky pin to the stable model (no :canary tag). uses admin privileges.

sam: if they need immediate mitigation and they don't have admin access, they can add `model=redwood-xl-3` in their request to override routing. not ideal long-term but fast.

maya: customer ran the header curl and returned response headers + body. attached here (sanitized). headers include `x-rw-reqid: rw-20260315-9f2` and `x-backend-trace: be-77a3`. body was 502 with "upstream read timeout".

diego: thanks. that's helpful — the x-backend-trace points to the canary pool instance. ops-bot: can you check if any canary host was OOM or throttling around 10:10-10:20?

ops-bot: I've pulled infra metrics — a single canary shard saw GPU memory pressure and queued spikes at 10:11, causing a brief queue overflow (10:11:05 - 10:12:40). connected traces: be-77a3 on host canary-gpu-12.

lee: that aligns with the 502s. expected behavior: routing policy should fallback to stable when canary instances are unhealthy if fallback is enabled. do we have fallback enabled for acme?

diego: checking routing config for tenant acme... (reading) — fallback policy = enabled, but the rollout had a model variant mismatch for KV cache config which caused some canary kernels to fail on certain sequence lengths. kernel failures trigger 502 rather than graceful fallback in that codepath.

sam: ok so actionable items: 1) Ask customer to pin to stable (if ok) OR we pin for them. 2) Provide debug bundle for deeper analysis (we need host logs + trace). 3) Build a small repro that hits that sequence length / quantization path.

maya: customer asked whether pinning is safe — they're fine with short-term pin. they asked for step-by-step for pin.

diego: I've created an internal short-term rollback runbook: 
- run admin pin command (last pinned to stable)
- monitor 1xx/5xx rates for 10m
- if stable normal, schedule canary rollback and re-upload canary with kernel fix.

sam: maya — send customer this minimal guidance to pin themselves (or ask us to do it): 
1) add `"model":"redwood-xl-3"` to requests OR
2) we can perform tenant pin (requires admin key).

maya: sent pin steps and curl with X-Request-ID and X-RW-Debug. customer accepted us doing the pin.

maya: ops — can you pin them now and confirm?

ops-bot: Tenant pin applied for acme -> redwood-xl-3 at 10:28 PDT. monitoring.

ops-bot: after pin, 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 2 minutes.

maya: customer confirmed latency back to normal after pin. said they'd be fine with a canary rollback while eng digs into kernel mismatch.

diego: I'll reproduce locally using the exact sequence length and quantization flags and push a fix. will post repro steps and a patched canary later today.

sam: thanks all. please attach the debug bundle + the host trace id to the ticket (rw-20260315-9f2, be-77a3). closing loop with customer once canary patched. :thumbsup:

maya: noted. will attach bundles and update the ticket. 

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2124 updated with pin action and debug bundle request.
